name: Tongariro National Park
blurb: Volcanic tussock plateau where whio and falcons face stoats and possums.

tip.title: Remove the stoats
tip.text: Stoats raid blue duck nests and kill falcons, pigeons and tomtits. Set Stoat to -100% and watch the birds recover, then the hares and possums they eat.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Tongariro National Park, Blue duck, New Zealand falcon). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: Introduced for grouse shooting, it now covers over a third of the park and has displaced native plants. Red deer eat it.

nodes.name: Broadleaf (kapuka)
nodes.desc: A native broadleaf tree whose leaves and fruit are eaten by possums, pigeons and tūī.

nodes.name: River algae (periphyton)
nodes.desc: The slimy film of algae on stream stones. It feeds the insect larvae that blue ducks scour from the riverbed.

nodes.name: Red deer
nodes.desc: Introduced browser listed among the park's pests. It eats heather and also browses other plants; carcasses feed scavengers.
Introduced from Australia; mostly eats leaves, flowers and fruit but also takes bird eggs and chicks. Seen as a major threat to native forests and birds.
Introduced grazer and the most-recorded mammal near the park. Eaten by falcons, harriers and stoats.
Cased caddisfly larvae are named by Wikipedia as a main food of blue ducks in fast, clean mountain streams.

nodes.name: Swamp harrier (kāhu)
nodes.desc: Open-country hawk recorded near the park that hunts and also scavenges carrion; GloBI records hares, rabbits and possums as prey.
Introduced predator and a major threat to blue ducks; it kills nesting birds and takes hares, possums and even falcons in GloBI records.
Drives growth from the forest to the alpine zone, where altitude sets the plant belts.
Rain and snow on the volcanic peaks feed the forests, tussock lands and cold fast rivers.
Fungi and soil invertebrates recycle dead leaves and carcasses into the soil.

story: Tongariro National Park in the central North Island is New Zealand's oldest national park and the sixth established in the world. Its active volcanoes are Ruapehu, Ngauruhoe and Tongariro. It is a World Heritage Site for mixed cultural and natural values.
matters: Many of its summits, including Ngauruhoe and Ruapehu, are tapu, or sacred, to Māori. Habitats range from temperate rainforest to alpine ecosystems.
